Prepossessing

/pree-puh-ZESS-ing/ · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Prepossessing means creating a favorable impression — attractive or appealing in appearance or manner, especially at first sight

Prepossessing means creating a favorable first impression — attractive or appealing in looks or manner. The bakery's prepossessing window display, with its rows of glossy fruit tarts, drew customers inside before they had read a single review.

Worked Example

The new intern had such a prepossessing manner — a warm smile, easy confidence, and genuine attention to everyone she met — that the whole office liked her by lunchtime.

Her smile, confidence, and attentiveness create an immediately favorable impression, which is exactly what prepossessing describes: winning people over at first encounter.

How Prepossessing Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

appealing

appealing: attractive and pleasing

charming

charming: delightfully pleasing in manner

engaging

engaging: winning attention and goodwill

Antonyms

off-putting

off-putting: creating an unpleasant impression

unappealing

unappealing: not attractive or inviting

How Strong Is It? — pleasant → captivating → prepossessing

pleasant vs. prepossessing

pleasant vs. prepossessing: Pleasant describes anything mildly agreeable; prepossessing is stronger, suggesting looks or manner that actively win people over the moment they meet you.

captivating vs. prepossessing

captivating vs. prepossessing: Captivating goes further than prepossessing — it means holding someone completely spellbound, not just making a good first impression.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — pre-

Prefix — pre-: before, in advance (Latin prae-)

Root — possess

Root — possess: to occupy, take hold of (Latin possidere)

Suffix — -ing

Suffix — -ing: forms adjectives from verbs

Put it together

Put it together: Pre- (before) + possess (to occupy, take hold of): something prepossessing takes hold of your good opinion before you have had time to judge — it occupies your mind favorably in advance.

Use the root in a new word: repossess

Use the root in a new word: repossess: The bank threatened to repossess the delivery van after three missed payments — literally to take possession of it back.

Word Choice

Formal / slightly old-fashioned

Prepossessing most often describes a person's appearance or manner, frequently in the phrases 'a prepossessing manner' or, in the negative, 'not very prepossessing.' It is about first impressions — use it when someone or something wins favor on sight, not after long acquaintance.
